summary: Anthropic published a case study on the Government of Alberta using Claude Code (Opus and Sonnet models) with parallel autonomous agents to scan 466 million lines of government code for security vulnerabilities, remediate them, and run continuous red-team/blue-team security review.

practices.reason: The two-stage scan-then-review pipeline with dozens of parallel autonomous agents and file/line-cited findings is a concrete multi-agent design a team could adapt, though the exact implementation is tied to Alberta's own codebase and infrastructure.
practices.quote: Around 50 agents worked autonomously and in parallel to scan the systems for security vulnerabilities, weaknesses in underlying infrastructure and deployment processes, and gaps in technical documentation. Claude Code ran a two-stage routine, first scanning each repository with a rules engine to flag known patterns, then reviewing those flags and citing the exact file and line for each finding so developers could verify them.

practices.reason: The red team/blue team agent pattern that checks every application against a fixed set of security controls is a transferable evaluation methodology for judging whether a system meets a security bar.
practices.quote: A “red team” agent probes an application from the outside, the way an attacker might, and maps how a vulnerability might be exploited. A “blue team” agent then assesses the application’s defenses against an international security standard, and writes a remediation plan that points to the exact files to fix. ... Every application is checked against roughly 95 security controls on each pass.
